svg.title: APL's inhibition of the Kenyon cells as a slow conductance, against flies' limits and time course
svg.text: APL as a conductance: graded like flies', within flies' limits, and as slow as flies'
APL's synapses onto the Kenyon cells reverse 20 mV below each cell's rest and fade over 0.3 s: APL answers 4-methylcyclohexanol with 0.53 of its 3-octanol peak (flies 0.49),
silencing it raises the Kenyon cells' spikes 2.7- and 2.7-fold (flies 2-3), and it never holds them past 5.4 mV during an odor (as a current: 21).
The Kenyon cells' inhibition as 3-octanol begins
